task.name: forge groom --apply reports a body restructure on a bug that carries an acceptance-criteria section but leaves the section in place, so shape and diagnose keep refusing the issue
task.story_text:
## Observed

On 2026-09-18, issue #2090 (a bug with no type label whose body carried an `## Acceptance criteria` checklist) was run through the intake surfaces in sequence. `forge diagnose` investigated it at $0.73 and then refused to land, evaluated `needs_type`. `forge shape 2090 --apply` refused with a blocking `type_shape_contradiction` finding naming the acceptance-criteria section. `forge groom 2090 --apply` exited 0, printed pre-groom and post-groom verdicts both `needs_type`, and reported "Applied body restructure to #2090", but the issue body afterward still contained the same `## Acceptance criteria` section with its three bullets, and a second `forge shape --apply` refused with the identical finding. No forge surface could move the issue out of that state; the section was removed by hand, after which shape applied the type label and diagnose became runnable.

## Expected

When a typed-intake surface identifies the one structural defect that keeps an issue from advancing, the surface designated to repair structure either repairs it or reports that it cannot and says which surface can. A groom that changes nothing about the finding it was invoked to clear does not report a restructure as applied, and no sequence of shape, groom and diagnose leaves an issue in a state that only a hand edit can exit.

## Diagnosis

**Baseline:** `0013248f13ef525225550a0f39eaba1a95446152` captured at `2026-09-18T13:59:15.918340+00:00`

**Inspected files:**

- `src/theforge/intake/groom_flow.py` — `sha256:b5399736e8eaa58244a0f271702bb07d08bc079a438c02cf8e9a3d8f38198c78`
- `src/theforge/cli/groom.py` — `sha256:462ff5e114644d88d6da866c5e784007f75c7092d26b7d3aa4944d393d75b707`
- `src/theforge/shape_check/check.py` — `sha256:bda01187ce9e8d51fde400454000d6b9e5ec9cc3f4b6c20c9272a5cdb4bd42eb`
- `src/theforge/shape_check/heuristics.py` — `sha256:a561105c9404398bfdade2a015b04e55c72f53217e41fe5041ce7fd69c1e071f`
- `.forge/audits/diagnose-issue-2090-e91e5629260c.yaml` — `sha256:5626ec63244e9a2ef0d38fdcc4d4e5fc4dfe944171c53d4d7b37d6c98ebb7a90`
- `.forge/audits/diagnose-issue-2090-db38c3f1fff1.yaml` — `sha256:066acbfb4cd765f02d81b1e4644bb679dc8931aecf0d93e0ca41a3e206836990`

### Observed symptom

`forge groom --apply` on a bug-shaped issue that has no recognized type label
and whose body already carries a `## Acceptance criteria` section reports
"Applied body restructure" and `applied=True`, but the AC section is left
completely untouched and no type label is added. Pre- and post-groom shape
verdicts are identical (`needs_type`), so the issue is exactly as blocked
after groom as before it, despite groom's success-shaped report.

### Reproduction / evidence

Reproduced locally at HEAD (release/v0.16) by calling
`theforge.intake.groom_flow.run_groom` with injected fetch/edit stubs
returning a bug-shaped body (`## Observed` / `## Expected` / `##
Acceptance criteria` with three checklist bullets) and `labels=[]` (no
type label):
  - `res.issue_type` -> `None`
  - `res.bug_state` -> `BugDiagnosisState.NOT_A_BUG`
  - `res.action` -> `GroomAction.RESTRUCTURED`
  - `res.pre_verdict` / `res.post_verdict` -> both `ShapeVerdict.NEEDS_TYPE`
  - `res.applied` -> `True`
  - `res.proposed_body` — identical to the original body plus an appended
    `## Example` placeholder stub; the `## Acceptance criteria` section and
    its three bullets are byte-identical to the input, untouched.
`src/theforge/cli/groom.py:120-127` prints "Applied body restructure" purely
because `result.needs_change` (`proposed_body != original_body`) is true —
it does not check whether any blocking finding was actually resolved. Since
`_restructure_feature_body` happened to add an unrelated `## Example` stub
(the AC heading was already present so no AC-related edit ever occurs), the
CLI reports success even though the two findings that actually block the
issue (`missing_type`, and — once a `bug` label lands — `type_shape_contradiction`)
are never addressed.
I could not use the live GitHub issue #2090 cited in the report as a direct
repro target: its current body/labels (`bug` label, full `## Diagnosis`
section, no `## Acceptance criteria` at all) match a real, different,
already-diagnosed bug about RCA misclassification
(`.forge/audits/diagnose-issue-2090-*.yaml`, `issue_title` = "Pre-dev rebase
conflict misclassified as unknown_needs_rca..."). #2090 has evidently been
reused/overwritten since the #3054 report's reproduction, so I reconstructed
the reported scenario directly against `groom_flow.run_groom` instead.

### Hypotheses tested

- **[confirmed]** `_classify_action` has no branch for an issue whose type cannot be detected (`issue_type is None`); it falls through every `issue_type == "bug"` guard to the unconditional final `return GroomAction.RESTRUCTURED, None`, so an untyped issue is always classified as a normal, successful restructure regardless of what actually needs fixing.
  - Evidence: groom_flow.py:439-475 (`_classify_action`): every conditional branch requires `issue_type == "bug"`; there is no `issue_type is None` case, so it always reaches the trailing `return GroomAction.RESTRUCTURED, None` at line 475. Reproduced directly: passing `labels=[]` yields `res.action == GroomAction.RESTRUCTURED`.
  - Claim verification: verified against source and attached evidence. Read groom_flow.py directly and confirmed the same result by executing run_groom() against a constructed repro body/labels.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Directly read the source and directly executed the repro in this investigation; not a restatement of the issue report.
- **[confirmed]** For the RESTRUCTURED action, the body-edit dispatch only special-cases `issue_type == "bug"` (normalize only); every other value including `None` falls to `_restructure_feature_body`, which only inserts an AC or Example stub *when the heading is absent* — it never edits, relocates, or removes an existing (and, for a bug, contradictory) `## Acceptance criteria` section.
  - Evidence: groom_flow.py:571-578 dispatches to `_restructure_feature_body` for any non-"bug" issue_type. `_restructure_feature_body` (groom_flow.py:275-292) guards each stub insertion with `if not find_heading(...)`; since the AC heading is already present, that branch is skipped entirely and the section survives byte-for-byte. Reproduced: `res.proposed_body` contains the original AC section verbatim, with only an appended, unrelated `## Example` stub.
  - Claim verification: verified against source and attached evidence. Read _restructure_feature_body source directly and confirmed behavior by executing it against a body that already has an AC section.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Directly observed in this investigation's repro run.
- **[confirmed]** The CLI's "Applied body restructure" message is gated only on whether the proposed body differs from the original (`needs_change`), not on whether the specific blocking finding the surface was invoked to clear was actually resolved — so a body edit that is wholly unrelated to the blocking finding (here, the appended Example stub) still prints as a successful repair.
  - Evidence: src/theforge/cli/groom.py:120-127: `if result.needs_change: ... print("Applied body restructure" ...)` — no correlation with pre_verdict/post_verdict or with which finding codes changed.
  - Claim verification: verified against the target repository source. Read groom.py directly.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Directly observed in this investigation.
- **[ruled out]** Live GitHub issue #2090 is still in the exact broken state the report describes and can be used to directly reproduce the symptom end-to-end via the real CLI.
  - Evidence: gh issue view 2090 shows a `bug`-labeled issue with a complete `## Diagnosis`/confirmed-cause section about RCA misclassification and no `## Acceptance criteria` section at all — a different, already-live bug. `.forge/audits/diagnose-issue-2090-db38c3f1fff1.yaml` and `-e91e5629260c.yaml` (issue_number: 2090) confirm this same title/content as a genuine diagnose run, not the #3054 reproduction artifact.
  - Claim verification: verified against source and attached evidence. Fetched the live issue via `gh issue view` and cross-checked against on-disk diagnose audit records for the same issue number.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Directly observed; not inferred from the #3054 report text.

### Confirmed cause

`groom_flow._classify_action` (src/theforge/intake/groom_flow.py:439-475) has
no explicit branch for an issue whose type could not be detected
(`issue_type is None`, i.e. no recognized type label present). Every
branch in the function is gated on `issue_type == "bug"`; an untyped issue
falls through all of them to the unconditional default `return
GroomAction.RESTRUCTURED, None`. `run_groom`'s subsequent body-edit dispatch
(groom_flow.py:571-578) then routes any non-"bug" `issue_type` — including
`None` — to `_restructure_feature_body` (groom_flow.py:275-292), whose only
behavior is to insert a stub `## Acceptance criteria` or `## Example`
section *when the corresponding heading is missing*; it never edits or
removes an existing section. For a bug-shaped issue that already carries an
`## Acceptance criteria` section (the very content that keeps it blocked —
first by `missing_type`, then, once a `bug` label is present, by
`type_shape_contradiction`), the only edit `_restructure_feature_body` makes
is inserting an unrelated missing `## Example` stub. That edit alone is
enough to make `proposed_body != original_body`, so `run_groom` reports
`action=RESTRUCTURED`, `applied=True`, and the CLI (cli/groom.py:120-127)
prints "Applied body restructure" — while the pre- and post-groom shape
verdicts stay identical (`needs_type`) because nothing that determines
either the missing-type or the contradictory-section finding was ever
touched. No label is added, and the AC section is never removed or
relabeled, so a second `forge shape --apply` refuses again with the same
finding, and there is no sequence of groom/shape/diagnose invocations that
can move the issue forward without a hand edit.

Claim verification: verified against source and attached evidence. Read groom_flow.py and cli/groom.py directly, then confirmed the mechanism by executing run_groom() locally against a constructed repro body/labels combination matching the reported scenario.
Support: Direct execution of `run_groom()` against a constructed repro (bug-shaped
body with `## Observed`/`## Expected`/`## Acceptance criteria`, `labels=[]`)
reproduced exactly the reported shape: `issue_type=None`,
`action=GroomAction.RESTRUCTURED`, `pre_verdict=post_verdict=NEEDS_TYPE`,
`applied=True`, and a `proposed_body` whose AC section is byte-identical to
the input, with only an appended `## Example` stub as the sole diff. This is
independent, source-verified reproduction of the mechanism, not a
restatement of the issue's own narrative — the issue report did not name
`_classify_action`'s fallthrough or `_restructure_feature_body`'s
presence-only guard; those were traced here directly in groom_flow.py.
Support provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. The failing code paths and the repro output were both directly observed in this investigation; the live issue #2090 could not be used as a repro target since its content has since been overwritten by an unrelated, genuine bug diagnosis.
Independence note: This text uses independence/corroboration language. Verify the cited material is a second source rather than a prior assertion.

### Affected code path

src/theforge/intake/groom_flow.py:439-475 (`_classify_action` — no
`issue_type is None` branch; falls through to the default
`GroomAction.RESTRUCTURED`), groom_flow.py:571-578 (RESTRUCTURED dispatch
routes any non-"bug" issue_type, including `None`, to
`_restructure_feature_body`), groom_flow.py:275-292
(`_restructure_feature_body` — only inserts stub sections when the heading
is absent, never edits/removes an existing forbidden or contradictory
section); src/theforge/cli/groom.py:120-127 (prints "Applied body
restructure" based solely on `result.needs_change`, uncorrelated with
whether the blocking finding was resolved).

### Fix-success criterion

For a bug-shaped issue with no recognized type label whose body already
carries a section that would be forbidden once typed (e.g. `##
Acceptance criteria`), running `forge groom --apply` must either (a) leave
the issue's shape verdict changed to reflect real progress and never print
a success-shaped "Applied body restructure" message when the applied edit
did not change any blocking finding code between pre- and post-groom shape
results, or (b) explicitly refuse/report that it cannot repair this
condition and name the surface that can. After the fix, running
`forge groom --apply` then `forge shape --apply` in sequence on such an
issue must not reproduce the identical blocking finding twice in a row
with groom having reported success in between.

### Related findings (out of scope)

> These are adjacent problems noticed during investigation. They are **not** the cause of this issue's symptom and are **out of scope for this fix** — triage them separately under the linked issue. Do not implement them as part of this issue.

- `check_type_shape_contradiction` only fires when a type label is already declared (`_declared_type_spec` returns `None` for an untyped issue), so an untyped bug-shaped issue with a contradictory AC section only ever surfaces as generic `missing_type` until some other process adds a type label — the type_shape_contradiction finding itself doesn't appear until then. This is a separate shape-check sequencing question, not the groom defect this issue reports.

### Advisory repair proposal

> Advisory only: this is an unverified repair idea from the investigation, not part of the confirmed diagnosis contract.

Add an explicit `issue_type is None` branch to `_classify_action` — most
naturally REFUSED (mirroring the `NO_DIAGNOSIS` bug refusal), since groom
cannot safely restructure a body whose shape it can't determine, so the
operator is told to add a type label (or run whatever surface infers one)
before groom can act. If groom is meant to still land in RESTRUCTURED for
untyped issues, gate the "Applied body restructure" success message in
cli/groom.py on the set of finding codes that changed between
`pre_verdict`/`post_verdict` (or `pre_result.reasons`/`post_result.reasons`)
rather than on raw `needs_change`, so an edit that doesn't touch the
actually-blocking finding is reported honestly as insufficient.

### Notes

The report's own reproduction issue (#2090) is no longer in the state the
report describes — it currently holds a real, separately diagnosed bug
about RCA misclassification (confirmed via `gh issue view 2090` and the
on-disk `diagnose-issue-2090-*.yaml` audit records). This diagnosis is
therefore based on a direct code-level reconstruction of the reported
scenario rather than the live issue; the mechanism traced matches the
report's described symptom exactly (identical pre/post `needs_type`
verdicts, "Applied body restructure" printed, AC section left in place).
I did not verify the report's claim that a *second* `forge shape --apply`
after groom hits `type_shape_contradiction` specifically (vs. `needs_type`
again) — that would require a `bug` label to have been added between the
first and second shape runs (e.g. by an ambient GitHub Action labeler),
which is plausible but outside what I could observe directly; either way
the underlying groom defect (false-positive "applied" report, AC section
never touched) is the same.
